stage_a.note: Smiling, enthusiastic, clear positive engagement throughout.
Sustained engagement with the subject and animated delivery.
Friendly, considerate expression, smiling at the panel.

venture.description: A mobile audio entertainment app that uses geolocation to play narrated stories about landmarks and cities as users travel.
venture.note: A mobile app focused on road trips and travel.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 delivers the prepared pitch for Autio, an audio travel guide app triggered by geolocation.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks F1 to walk him through an example of how a customer buys and uses the app.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains that users download the free app, get five free stories, and then pay $36 for unlimited streaming.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks how long the audio stories are.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states the stories average three to four minutes, with some up to twenty minutes.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks what happens if a user is in a remote area without wifi or in a dense city.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains stories can be downloaded offline and are triggered automatically by the phone's GPS.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks about F1's background and how he started the company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 shares his 19-year background in software and his previous successful app company, iStoryTime.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks why F1 is offering only 5% for $1 million, implying a high $20 million valuation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains that strategic partners are investing at a higher valuation, so the Sharks are getting a discount.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks F1 to confirm that the company has sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms they have over $700,000 in sales this year and a $2 million annual run rate.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 acknowledges the sales figures as respectable.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks how much capital the company has raised so far.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they have raised $3.5 million and have strategic partnerships with a major auto club and RV retailer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks why F1 needs a Shark if he already has significant backing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains they need help spreading the word about their new product category.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks how many subscribers the app currently has.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they have 15,000 paid members and 210,000 registered accounts.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks what percentage of subscribers have renewed their memberships.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains that early subscribers renew at 70%, but the average renewal rate is about 50%.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks for confirmation that the attrition rate is 50%.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms the 50% rate, noting it is average for consumer subscription services.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 expresses surprise, stating he didn't know that was the average.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 exits, stating he is not a fan and believes competitors could easily replicate the feature.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 exits, feeling the $1 million ask is crazy compared to the 15,000 current subscribers.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 exits, finding F1 credible but not feeling excited enough about the business to invest.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 exits, viewing the app as a feature rather than a standalone consumer product.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks F1 to repeat the annual subscription fee.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 reiterates that the fee is $36 for one year and $70 for three years.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks what the company's customer acquisition cost is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states the average is $38, but it recently dropped under $10 due to word of mouth and awards.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks if F1 believes he can keep the acquisition cost down to $10.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confidently replies that they can maintain it at around $9.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 offers $1 million for a 15% stake, citing F1's credibility.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 emphasizes his value, offering to narrate stories and leverage his millions of followers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 expresses appreciation for S1's followers, agreeing it would help add subscribers.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks if there are other areas where his involvement would add value.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 agrees, noting that S1's reputation means everyone returns his calls.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 promises to open any doors F1 needs.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 counters S1's offer, proposing $1 million for a 6.5% stake.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 rejects 6.5% as too low and revises his offer to $1 million for 12%.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 counters with 7%.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 insists on 10% as his absolute minimum.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 reiterates that 7% is the absolute maximum equity he can offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 proposes a revised structure of 7% equity plus 3% in advisory shares to reach 10%.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains that using advisory shares is the only way he could exceed the 5% mark.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 reiterates his demand for 10% total to close the deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states he cannot accept the deal at that price.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 jokes that S1 is throwing F1's other investors under the bus.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 proudly embraces his Mr. Wonderful persona.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 argues that S1 is already getting a significant discount compared to other investors.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 deflects blame for the cap table and points out he already compromised from 15% to 10%.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 formally declines the 10% offer, ending the negotiation.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 praises F1 for sticking to his valuation.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 congratulates F1 on a great presentation.

decisions.note: Not a fan of the app; believes competitors like Google Maps could easily replicate it.
Thinks the $1 million valuation is crazy compared to the 15,000 subscriber count.
Finds the founder credible but is not excited enough about the business to invest.
Views the app as an immersive feature rather than a standalone consumer product.
Intrigued and finds the founder very credible; offers the requested amount for more equity.
Appreciates the offer but is only willing to go up slightly for the value add.
Rejects 6.5% as too low and drops his equity request to 12%.
Counters with 7%, moving slightly up from his previous offer.
States that 10% is the absolute minimum equity he will accept.
Tries to reach his 10% requirement by structuring it with advisory shares.
Declines the offer, stating he cannot give up 10% total equity.
